2.
The accident in the present case took place on 04.09.2017.
The petitioner Surender Kumar was returning to his house from hospital where his father was admitted.

When he reached at Vikas Marg,
Delhi near PP Jwellers, a scooty registration No.HR-14M-0395, which was driven by its driver respondent no. 1 Jung Sher Singh in a rash & negligent manner hit him.
Due to this accident, the petitioner suffered grievous injuries.
He was hospitalised for around six days.

Due to this accident,
he incurred permanent disability.
According to his disability certificate, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 14% in his left lower limb.

3. After completion of the investigation in the accident, the present Detail Accident Report (DAR)
was filed.

4. The respondent no. 1 Jung Sher Singh who is the driver and owner of the offending vehicle has replied stating that the accident did not take place from his vehicle and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
5. The respondent no. 2 insurance company - Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. has taken the general defences.

entities.text: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: It is also alleged that the respondent no. 1 was driving the vehicle without valid driving licence.

6. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties following issues were framed on 17.02.2019 :-
(i) Whether Mr. Surender suffered injuries in a motor vehicular accident on 04.09.2017 at about 8.30 p.m. at Vikas Marg, near PP Jewellers, Delhi within jurisdiction of PS Preet Vihar due to rash and negligent driving of motor vehicle bearing registration No. HR 14M 0395 (scooty) driven by the respondent No. 1 / Jung Sher Singh?(OPP)
(ii) Whether R1 / driver of the offending vehicle was holding a valid and effective driving licence to drive scooty bearing registration No. HR 14M 0395, if not, its effect?(OPR1)
(iii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation, if so,to what amount and from whom?(OPP)
(iv) Whether the petitioner is entitled to interest on the award amount, if so, at what rate and for which period?(OPP)
(v) Relief?
7. In order to establish his claim, petitioner Surender Kumar has examined himself as PW-1.

He also examined PW-2 Dr. Hemant Sharma, Specialist (Ortho), who has proved the disability certificate Ex.PW1/5 and assessment sheet Ex.PW2/A.

2 8.

entities.text: Surender vs Jung Sher Singh & Another

sentences.text:
In their defence, the respondent / insurance company has examined Rishabh Sahoo as RW1, who proved the copy of insurance police alongwith terms and condition Ex.RW1/1.
9.
I have heard Mr. Balram Singh, counsel for petitioner, Mr. Mahipal counsel for respondent no. 1 and Mr. Pranav Mishra counsel for respondent no. 2 and perused the records.

Issue No. 1 : Whether Mr. Surender suffered injuries in a motor vehicular accident on 04.09.2017 at about 8.30 p.m. at Vikas Marg, near PP Jewellers, Delhi within jurisdiction of PS Preet Vihar due to rash and negligent driving of motor vehicle bearing registration No. HR 14M 0395 (scooty) driven by the respondent No. 1 / Jung Sher Singh?(OPP)
10.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further in holding any inquiry under section 168, the Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
11. Now in this case, the petitioner is the eye-witness of the accident because he received injuries in the accident.

In order to establish his claim, he has examined himself as PW-1 and proved copy of his aadhar card Ex.PW1/1, voter ID card Ex.PW1/2, Detail Accident Report(DAR) Ex.PW1/3, salary account statement Ex.PW1/4, disability certificate Ex.PW1/5 and medical bills Mark-X.
He stated on oath in the affidavit about the accident and how it was caused.
He has clearly deposed that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent no.1, who was the driver of the offending vehicle.
He deposed that on on 04-09-2017, at about 08.30 PM, he after admitting his father in the Metro Hospital, Preet Vihar, Delhi was returning to his house.
When he reached Vikas Marg, Delhi near PP Jwellers, a scooty registration No. HR-14M-0395, which was driven by its driver respondent no. 1 Jung Sher Singh in a rash & negligent manner hit him.

Due to this accident,
he suffered grievous injuries.
According to his disability certificate, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 14% due to bimalleolar fracture of left ankle.
On 14.09.2017 he was admitted in Hedgewar Hospital.
His left ankle was operated on 15.09.2017 and thereafter on 20.09.2017 he was discharged from the hospital after treatment.
He was advised for removing the plates/screw in future.
He was working with "ROTO POWER PROJECT PVT. LTD" and getting a salary of Rs.11,480/- per month at the time of accident.

12. The medical documents and other treatment records of the petitioner as well as the disability certificate, makes it clear that he suffered 14% permanent disability due to fracture in his left lower limb.
Respondent no. 1 did not led any evidence to prove any contrary to the claim of the petitioner.

In the case of Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Cmpany Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3) AD Delhi 310 it was held that an adverse inference can be drawn when the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter into the witness box.

entities.text: Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Cmpany Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3) AD Delhi 310
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even the insurance company has not led any evidence to disprove the claim of the petitioner.
13. After investigation, the police filed the chargesheet against respondent no. 1 the driver of the scooty.

Filing of chargesheet against the driver of offending vehicle prima facie points to his Surender vs Jung Sher Singh & Another on 8 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192964887/
3 culpability.

entities.text: Surender vs Jung Sher Singh & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. In New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held that as a general rule, it can be accepted that production of chargesheet is prima facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of claim under section 166 MV Act.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If any party do not accept such chargesheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.

If the Tribunal feels that chargesheet is collusive, it can record that chargesheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the chargesheet.

15. In view of above, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities of evidence, it is proved that Surender Kumar suffered grievous injuries due to rash and negligent act of respondent no.1 Jung Sher Singh, the driver of the offending scooty.
Accordingly, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioners and against the respondents.

Issue No. 2 : Whether R1 / driver of the offending vehicle was holding a valid and effective driving licence to drive scooty bearing registration No. HR 14M 0395, if not, its effect?(OPR1)
16.
In his reply filed by the respondent no. 1, he has nowhere mentioned that he was driving the vehicle with any valid driving licence thereby admitting this fact.
Further, the detailed Accident Report of the investigating officer also states that the driver Jung Bahadur was not holding a valid driving licence.
The burden to prove the fact that he had a valid driving licence was upon the driver Jung Bahadur in the light of all other evidence against him which he failed to discharge.
He has not even appeared as a witness to prove that he had the licence on that day.
Therefore, adverse inference can be drawn against him.

Therefore, all these things clearly indicate and proves that respondent no.
1 Jung Bahadur was not holding the valid driving licence at the time of accident.
Accordingly, this issue is decided against the respondent no. 1.
Issue No. 3 : Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation on account of said injuries and if yes, to what extent and from whom?

(OPP) 
17. Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
18. The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held in this case that in routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under the heads-(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured , comprising (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment and (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation is Surender vs Jung Sher Singh & Another on 8 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192964887/
4 also to be done under the head of loss of future earnings which would depend the effect and impact of such permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured.

entities.text: Surender vs Jung Sher Singh & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.

What requires to be assessed by the tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of percentage of the income.
It has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings by applying standard multiplier method.
All injuries or permanent disabilities arising from injuries do not resulting loss of earning capacity.

If there is no loss of employment or earning capacity, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities in consequent to his injuries.
Now, in the present case, the injured Surender Kumar has suffered a fracture in his lower limb which caused a medical disability of 14%.
Therefore on the basis of the injuries to the petitioner, the compensation is awarded to him under the aforesaid heads as follows -

MEDICAL EXPENSES:
19.
Petitioner has not proved any medical bills on record.
He has admitted this fact in his cross examination also.
During arguments, it was apprised that his entire treatment was running in a government hospital, therefore, he did not have the medical bills.
Under this head, the actual medical bills are reimbursed.
Therefore, due to lack of any medical expenses, nothing can be granted under this head.

PAIN AND SUFFERING:
20.
After the accident, petitioner remained in hospital for around 6 days.
The petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in this case which was fracture of his left lower limb.
As per disability certificate, he suffered a permanent disability to the extent of 15% disability due to this fracture.
The nature of injuries and the disability suffered by him, is a clear proof of the amount of pain and suffering, he must have endured in that accident.

Accordingly, I find it appropriate to grant a sum of Rs.25,000/-
to the petitioner under this head.
CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES 21.
The petitioner has not proved any actual expenses in relation to these heads and has not placed any material on record to substantiate the said expenses.
In the given facts and circumstances of the case, I deem it fit to grant Rs.5,000/- to petitioner for conveyance and special diet charges.
22. Though no evidence has been led to show that petitioner had hired any attendant during his treatment and he has not claimed anything under this head.

It cannot be ignored that family members of petitioner must have had to render their services for providing assistance to the petitioner for his routine activities and that would definitely suffer their work/job.

For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the Surender vs Jung Sher Singh & Another on 8 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192964887/
5 petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.

entities.text: Surender vs Jung Sher Singh & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).
Therefore, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/- as attendant charges.
23. Thus, petitioner is granted a total compensation of Rs.10,000/- (5,000+5,000) under this head.
LOSS OF INCOME DURING TREATMENT :
24. Petitioner has claimed that he was working in Rotto Power Project Limited and earning Rs.11,480/- per month.

There is no contrary evidence against this and because this is even less than the minimum wages, there is no harm in believing that the petitioner must have been earning this much money as claimed by him.
Therefore, his income is taken as Rs.11,480/- per month.
The evidence of the petitioner shows that he remained hospitalized for around 6 days.
There is no evidence for how long the petitioner was unable to work.
But it is not difficult to presume that in case of fracture he must have been disabled from work for a least three months as this would have been the minimum time to heel his wound.
Therefore, I award Rs.11,480/-(11,480x3) as compensation under this head.
Therefore, his loss of income for three month is calculated as Rs.34,440/-.
LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO PERMANENT DISABILITY.
25. The next question that remains to be decided is the compensation with respect to the disability of the petitioner.
Under this head, it has to be seen that what could be the future loss of income on account of disability.
The disability certificate of Dr. Hedgewar Arogya Sansthan clearly shows that the petitioner is the case of 14% disability due fracture in relation to left lower limb.
Though the doctor has been examined but the petitioner has not narrated how this disability will come in way of reducing the efficiency of the work in which the petitioner is engaged.
He has also not proved that due to this injury his income has reduced.
But because he has 14% disability due to fracture in left lower limb, it is not difficult to assume that this disability will affect his day-to-day life and profession.
Therefore, I presume that the petitioner must have suffered at least 5% functional disability, also in carrying on with his profession.
In view of this, I believe that functional disability in relation to whole body of the petitioner must be considered as 5% for the purpose of assessing corresponding loss of income of petitioner.

On the basis of his income taken as Rs.11,480/- per month, the petitioner's annual income shall be Rs.1,37,760/-.
26.

The copy of Aadhar card of the petitioner shows the date of birth of petitioner was 02.08.1982,
which would mean that he was around 34 years of age at the time of accident and thus, multiplier of 16 would be applicable.

Further, an addition of income of injured for future prospects to the extent of 40% has to be considered as the age of the petitioner was under the age of 40 years (National Insurance Company Limited vs Pranay Sethi and others (2017) 16 SCC 680, Pappu Dev Yadav vs Naresh Kumar and others 2010 SCC online SC 752 and Sohan Lal vs. Taj Khan & Ors., 2019 ACJ 252, Rajasthan High Court).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Pappu Dev Yadav vs Naresh Kumar and others 2010 SCC online SC 752
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sohan Lal vs. Taj Khan & Ors., 2019 ACJ 252
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The yearly income of the petitioner has been assessed as Rs.1,37,760/-.
In this after adding 40% of the future prospects amounting to Rs.55,104/-, the yearly income with future prospects will become Rs.1,92,864/-.

In this, yearly income, a multiplier of 16 will make the Surender vs Jung Sher Singh & Another on 8 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192964887/
6 future income as 1,92,864x16= Rs.30,85,824/-.

entities.text: Surender vs Jung Sher Singh & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
5% loss of income due to 5% percent functional disability will mean that the overall loss of income to the petitioner shall be 5% of Rs.30,85,824/-
which will be Rs.1,54,291/.
Therefore, this amount is awarded to the petitioner under this head.
LOSS OF AMENITIES 27.
Further, the petitioner is granted Rs.10,000/- for loss of amenities.

28. Thus, the compensation awarded to the petitioner is summarised as under:-
 Sl. No. Head of compensation Amount  1 Medical Expenses Nil.
 2 Pain & Sufferings Rs.25,000/-
 3 Conveyance & Special diet Rs.5,000/-

4 Attendant charges Rs.5,000/-
 Loss of Income during Rs.34,440/-
 treatment  Loss of future income due to Rs.1,54,291/-
permanent disability

7 Loss of Amenities Rs.10,000/-
 TOTAL Rs.2,23,731/-
Issue No. 3 (iii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to interest on the award amount, if so, at what rate and for which period?
Petitioner has pursued his case diligently.
Therefore, he is entitled for interest @ 7% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization.

LIABILITY:
30.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents are liable to pay the compensation amount.
As insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured.

Counsel for insurance company has raised the issue of recovery rights against the respondent no.1 who was the owner and driver of the offending vehicle on the ground that the driver Jung Bahadur was not having a valid driving licence.
As proved in issue no. 2, the driver Jung Bahadur was not holding a valid driving licence at the time of accident, thereby entitling the insurance company to recover the compensation amount from him.

RELIEF:
31.

In view of the findings on above points, I as presiding officer of this Tribunal award a total compensation of Rs.2,33,731/- (Rs. Two Lakhs Thirty-Three Thousand, Seven Hundred and Thirty Surender vs Jung Sher Singh & Another on 8 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192964887/
7 One only) along with interest @ 6% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization in favour of petitioner against the respondent no.2 Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd.
